group.passage:
When people hear the name “Silk Road,” many picture a single long road stretching across Asia. In fact, it was a huge [[1]] of trade routes. For more than a thousand years, these routes [[2]] China with Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe.
The name itself came much later. A German scholar created it in the nineteenth century, choosing silk because it was the best-known product to travel west from China. Chinese silk was so [[3]] that wealthy Romans paid very high prices for it. Few traders, however, ever traveled the whole way. The trip was slow and [[4]], as travelers had to cross burning deserts and freezing mountains. Camels, which can go for days without drinking, carried heavy loads across the dry land.
The Silk Road carried far more than silk. In busy markets, merchants [[5]] silk for horses, spices, glass, and gold. Ideas and beliefs also [[6]] along these routes, carried by traders, monks, and other travelers. Buddhism, for example, is a [[7]] that began in India and reached China this way. The art of making paper, invented in China, slowly traveled west in the same way. Over time, it changed how people in many lands kept records and shared knowledge.
Many cities along the way grew rich from this trade. In these busy places, people from many lands lived side by side, and [[8]] visitors were a common sight. In the thirteenth century, the Italian traveler Marco Polo spent many years in China, and the stories he [[9]] home with him made many Europeans curious about the East. Today, the Silk Road remains a powerful [[10]] of how trade can bring different cultures together.

translation_zh.text:
聽到「絲路」這個名稱時，許多人會想像一條橫越亞洲的漫長道路。事實上，它是由許多貿易路線組成的龐大網絡。一千多年來，這些路線把中國和中亞、中東以及歐洲連接在一起。
「絲路」這個名稱其實出現得晚得多。它是一位德國學者在十九世紀取的，他選用「絲」，是因為絲綢是從中國往西運送的商品中最有名的一種。中國絲綢非常珍貴，有錢的羅馬人願意付很高的價錢購買。不過，很少有商人走完全程。旅程緩慢又艱辛，旅人必須穿越酷熱的沙漠和嚴寒的高山。駱駝可以好幾天不喝水，負責馱著沉重的貨物穿越乾燥的土地。
絲路運送的遠不只絲綢。在熱鬧的市集裡，商人用絲綢交換馬匹、香料、玻璃和黃金。思想與信仰也沿著這些路線傳播，由商人、僧侶和其他旅人帶著走。例如，佛教就是一個起源於印度、經由這條路傳到中國的宗教。中國發明的造紙術也用同樣的方式慢慢往西傳。久而久之，它改變了許多地方的人保存紀錄和分享知識的方式。
沿途許多城市因這種貿易而致富。在這些熱鬧的地方，來自各地的人比鄰而居，外國訪客隨處可見。十三世紀時，義大利旅行家馬可‧波羅在中國待了許多年，他帶回家鄉的故事讓許多歐洲人對東方充滿好奇。今天，絲路仍是一個有力的象徵，代表貿易如何讓不同的文化彼此交流。
